description: The plot illustrates the training loss over steps for six different model configurations—ChemBART Small 20M, ChemBART Medium 20M, ChemBERTa Small 20M, ChemBERTa Medium 20M, ChemLLaMA Small 20M, and ChemLLaMA Medium 20M—all trained on a 20M data size. The x-axis, labeled “Step,” spans from 0K to 440K, with major tick marks at 0K, 20K, 40K, 60K, 80K, 420K, 430K, and 440K, indicating a non-uniform scale that compresses the later training phase. The y-axis, labeled “Train Loss,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.85, with grid lines at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.75, and 0.85. All six lines begin near 0.85 at 0K steps and exhibit a steep decline in loss within the first 20K steps, followed by a slower, gradual decrease toward convergence. By 80K steps, all models have reached a loss below 0.2, and by 440K steps, losses stabilize near 0.05–0.10. ChemLLaMA Small 20M (purple) and ChemLLaMA Medium 20M (brown) consistently show the lowest loss across most of the training trajectory, while ChemBERTa Small 20M (green) and ChemBERTa Medium 20M (orange) exhibit slightly higher losses, particularly in the early and mid-training phases. ChemBART Small 20M (red) and ChemBART Medium 20M (blue) follow similar trajectories, with ChemBART Medium 20M generally performing slightly better than its small counterpart. The inset zooms in on the 420K–440K step range, showing that all models have nearly converged, with minimal variation in loss values.
